newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 22-month high on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 22-month high on electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices roared to a 22-month high close on Friday as a recent bull run revived on active buying in the heavily weighted financial sector and fundamentals-backed electronic shares, brokers said.
The weighted index ended 68.90 points or 1.03 percent higher at 6,761.39, its highest finish since January 11, 1995.
Turnover was a hectic T$105 billion, the largest single-day volume since June 14.
Recently red-hot electronics soared by 2.37 percent while financials gained 1.88 percent.

The overall market has gained nearly 200 points in the past seven sessions despite Thursday's downturn, wich was triggered by a daylight gangland-style execution of a county magistrate and seven others that shocked investors.

"The killings put some fear in the market about Taiwan's overall security, but the effect was only momentary and the market picked itself up today," said Allen Huang, a manager at National Securities.
Brokers have said the current bull run has been fuelled in part by politically motivated, state-linked buying marking the six-month anniversary of President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration.
"The index has succesfully broken through strong resistance and investors are growing more confident about the market's prospect to rise more," National's Huang said.
Huang said the apparent start of year-end window dressing by local securities investment trust funds added more momentum to investors' bullish sentiment.

Recently listed electronic shares Inventec Corp and Asustek continued their honeymoon bounce. Inventec soared by the daily seven percent limit or T$10 to T$153. Asustek also ended limit up -- its eighth in as many sessions -- gaining T$11 to T$182.
Brokers expected the market to continue challenging for new highs in the coming week. The next resistance is seen at the 7,000 level.
A 6,730-6,840 range was seen for Saturday's abbreviated session.
